ST-04.title: Consolidated dark-mode contrast audit across shipped pages
ST-04.notes: Consolidated dark-theme-only pass across all 23 pages / 146+ component files (delegated to a sub-agent for systematic grep+read verification). 1 finding: src/components/ui/PageHeader.js title gradient had dark:from-/dark:to- overrides but no dark:via- pairing, so the via-stop fell through to the light-mode slate-700 value in dark theme (washed-out segment in page-title heading text, used by 21/23 pages). Classified TRIVIAL per decision_record.md §4 (single class-token swap) and fixed directly — added dark:via-slate-300. No non-trivial findings, so no consolidated backlog filing required (AC's 'or fixed directly if trivial' branch satisfied). Playwright coverage added (tests/e2e/page-header-dark-gradient-contrast.spec.js, SC-PHDG-01/02) per CLAUDE.md §2 frontend testing gate — written and reasoned against Tailwind's resolved rgb() computed-style values (verified hex-to-rgb math), but NOT locally executed: this sandbox's OS (ubuntu26.04) is unsupported by the installed Playwright version, blocking local chromium install. Will be confirmed in CI (playwright.yml) at PR open.

ST-03.title: Contrast/focus-state accessibility pass on v7.7 notification UX
ST-03.notes: Manual accessibility audit of in-scope v7.7 notification/digest surface (StandingAlert/StandingAlertStack, NotificationTabBar, NotificationRow, nav alert-count badge, Notifications page empty state) against design_system.md's WCAG AA text-contrast token and the new >=3:1 focus-indicator standard. No custom focus-ring overrides exist anywhere in scope -> focus-indicator criterion trivially satisfied (default browser/Tailwind ring applies unmodified). 1 finding: nav alert-count badge (src/Layout.js, both collapsed-group-header and item-level instances) used bg-red-500 with white count text = 3.76:1 contrast, below WCAG AA 4.5:1 (badge text 8-9px, does not qualify for large-text exemption). Classified TRIVIAL per decision_record.md §4 and fixed directly -- bg-red-500 -> bg-red-600 (4.83:1), both instances. Updated stale selectors in tests/e2e/alert-nav-badge.spec.js (cross-spec selector check, LL-v3.2-P3-02) and docs/testing/alert_nav_badge_scenarios.md SC-ANB-VIS-01 in the same commit. Documented in docs/specs/frontend/pages/notifications.md changelog (v0.7). No non-trivial findings -> no consolidated backlog filing required. New Playwright coverage (tests/e2e/notification-badge-contrast.spec.js, SC-BC-01/02) written but not locally executed -- same sandbox OS limitation as EPIC-04 (Playwright chromium install unsupported on this ubuntu26.04 sandbox); will run in CI at PR open. Rebase note: branched from main before EPIC-04 merged -- design_system.md shared-file dependency (ST-03 depends on ST-04 per sprint_backlog.md) needs a rebase once EPIC-04's PR actually merges.

ST-09.title: Extract shared retry/backoff decorator and migrate highest-traffic call site
ST-09.notes: Extracted shared retry/backoff decorator (backend/utils/retry.py, retry_with_backoff) -- configurable max_attempts/base_delay/max_delay/backoff_factor, injectable sleep_fn for testability, filters on retryable_exceptions so non-transient errors (e.g. ValueError for 'no data found') propagate immediately without wasting retries. Migrated the highest-traffic external call site per RISK-02: utils/pricing.py's _yahoo_get_current_price (used by every get_current_price() call -- all US-ticker Alpaca-fallback and all UK-ticker fetches; confirmed higher-traffic than Alpaca via call-site count, 9 consumer files vs Alpaca's 2, and Yahoo previously had ZERO retry logic vs Alpaca's existing hand-rolled retry). Restructured into an inner _yahoo_fetch_price (decorated, raises on failure) wrapped by the original _yahoo_get_current_price (catches, logs, returns None) -- external contract for all callers unchanged. No full retrofit of alpaca_service.py this cycle per RISK-02 scope bound -- remaining call sites migrate incrementally in future cycles. 9 new unit tests (tests/test_retry_backoff.py) all pass; full regression run across 7 consumer test files (193 tests total) confirms no behavioural regression.

ST-07.notes: New consolidated docs/ops/api_key_rotation_and_audit_schedule.md, building on alpaca_key_rotation_policy.md's pattern, covering all 5 named key types. 3 have real credentials with concrete first-rotation dates (Alpaca, Claude/Anthropic, Telegram); 2 (Yahoo Finance, Gemini) verified to have NO actual credential in this codebase -- Yahoo Finance uses only a User-Agent header on public endpoints, and 'Gemini' is a legacy filename (gemini_service.py) that calls only the Anthropic API (per the existing ESC-EXEC-20260720-01 finding in database.py). Adds a new quarterly audit cadence distinct from rotation (confirms credential still in use/minimally scoped/compliantly stored, or for the 2 no-credential entries, confirms that remains true). ST-08.title: Identify and remediate endpoints with no documented rate limit

sign_off_record.notes: First review Blocked on an arithmetic defect in the scope note (44/126 claimed vs actual 46/128 main.py endpoints) -- corrected in-session (verified independently via grep before editing) and re-reviewed to Approved. All 4 code changes and 5 tests independently verified against the actual files/test run, not taken on faith.

ST-08.notes: Full endpoint audit across all 128 live endpoints (82 in routers/*.py + 46 in main.py -- flagged as a scope discrepancy vs the story's stated '82', since main.py's endpoints are outside routers/*.py but clearly within the story's intent). Bucketed: 2 already rate-limited (AI daily-briefing/chat), 1 unauthenticated+unlimited (GET /health -- remediated, 60/min/IP via new _public_limiter), 3 authenticated Claude-calling endpoints previously unlimited (remediated, 10/min/IP each via existing _ai_limiter pattern: journal-summary, generate-plan, generate-thesis), 6 other external-API-calling endpoints accepted as lower-priority risk with per-endpoint rationale (not silently skipped), 116 plain DB endpoints accepted in bulk per RISK-04 (key-compromise threat model, covered by EPIC-07's rotation policy). Agent-mediated Cybersecurity & Trust Lead review caught a real arithmetic defect in the initial draft (44/126 vs actual 46/128) on first pass -- corrected and re-approved. 5 new unit tests (tests/test_rate_limit_endpoints.py) all pass; full regression (759 tests) confirms no behavioural change to any other endpoint.

ST-12.title: Add CI lint step for API contract heading-level compliance
ST-12.notes: New scripts/lint_api_contract_headings.py scans docs/specs/api_contracts/*.md for any HTTP-method+path-shaped heading NOT at exactly the canonical ## (depth-2) level -- unlike the existing openapi-drift.yml gate, which only matches literal '## ' and silently ignores any other depth (the exact documented CLAUDE.md §2 silent-fail case). Added as a new step in openapi-drift.yml running BEFORE the existing drift-detection step (satisfies 'runs ahead of/alongside'). Running the new lint against the REAL contracts directory surfaced one genuine pre-existing false-positive-looking case (two depth-3 headings in ai_advisory_contract_checklist.md) -- investigated and confirmed these are legitimate nested subsections of a checklist template (not orphaned top-level contract declarations; the real canonical contract for those endpoints is ai_endpoints.md), so added a documented, narrow NON_CANONICAL_FILES exemption (single file, single reason) rather than broadening the regex to something less precise. 7 unit tests (tests/test_lint_api_contract_headings.py) including the required negative test (a deliberately ###-miscoded heading, confirmed caught) and a regression guard that the real contracts directory lints clean today. Full suite (761 tests) passes.

ST-10.title: Define and apply flaky-test quarantine mechanism
ST-10.notes: New docs/testing/flaky_test_quarantine_process.md defines the quarantine mechanism: Playwright's built-in test.fixme(condition, description) with a required 'FLAKY-QUARANTINE: <reason> -- tracked in BLG-QA-<id>' description format, distinct from the existing deterministic environment-conditional test.skip() pattern already used in tests/e2e/keyboard-shortcuts.spec.js and visual-snapshots.spec.js (confirmed via scan neither is actually flaky -- both are legitimate environment-conditional skips, not migration candidates). Added tests/test_flaky_quarantine_format.py (5 tests) enforcing the format at the repo level -- any future test.fixme without the required prefix + backlog reference fails CI, preventing an untracked quarantine from silently accumulating. Repo-wide scan confirmed no currently-known flaky test exists to migrate (AC's 'if one exists' condition is not met today -- vacuously satisfied, documented explicitly in the process doc rather than silently omitted). Full regression suite passes.
